facts.fact: BEMA, an integrated judicial management system, was developed by the company JBSOFT Gabon with magistrates and court auxiliaries and presented by its designer, Jonas Beyeni, at a seminar in Libreville on 10 January 2026; the document states no adoption by the police, the gendarmerie or a ministry.

As its designer describes it, BEMA is built so that the judicial police officer enters the procedure and the software generates the procès-verbal, in a single file per person from arrest to release, passed digitally to the court and the prison; this is the design as presented on 10 January 2026, and the document states no station using it.

BEMA was officially presented on 10 January 2026 at a seminar in Libreville of magistrates and court auxiliaries; the designer says that police, court and prison currently work in isolation, with information re-entered at each; no deployment or adoption decision is stated.

systems.country_label: BEMA, système de gestion judiciaire intégré
systems.platform: ERP by JBSOFT Gabon, designed to run on ANINF's secured network
systems.tiers: none stated; presented at a seminar, designed for police, courts and prisons

note: The year of '10 janvier dernier' is read from the document's published date (2026-01). BEMA is also designed as an exchange link from police to court and prison; presented only, not stated as in use.
